prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-ZOE / Zoe: six-year-old human girl, deep brown skin, black hair in two puffs, yellow T-shirt, plum overalls, white sneakers. The ONLY named human protagonist is Zoe. Kit MUST NOT appear. Ignore every other child shown in reference sheets; unnamed adults may appear only when this scene explicitly requires them. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Light Where We Need It; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: One ordinary house porch and short flat path at dusk and night. WD-ZOE observes with an unnamed adult: light-brown skin, short gray hair, plain green shirt, dark pants, about 1.7 times Zoe's height. All fixture fitting is performed by the adult with power switched off, not modeled as a child task.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): One porch lamp with warm-colored bulb and removable fitted opaque top-and-side shield; its open lower face directs light down; Short path between front gate and porch; low hedge beside it; One upstairs window belonging to same house; Wall light switch and timer control inside doorway
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: One warm bulb; no dazzling beams into eyes or artificial daytime sky.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Unshielded lamp illuminates path and spills visibly onto upper window and hedge; Zoe with adult on porch.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions. CRITICAL PHYSICAL SETTING: show an ordinary two-story house with an UNCOVERED front stoop/porch, no porch roof, canopy, overhead beam, overhang or awning between lamp and upstairs window. One simple front door left; lamp right of door at adult-reachable height; upstairs window directly above lamp. Bare-bulb light can physically reach exterior window frame and nearby hedge along unobstructed straight paths. Upstairs room stays DARK, window glass dark navy, no interior illumination at opening. The removable opaque shade is shown separately as a design prop, open at bottom only. One location key plus separate adult/Zoe lineup and lamp details, no repetitive alternate houses. Adult should be about1.7 times Zoe height; no Kit. Everything flat clean cartoon.

visualReview.note: Generated source and installed WebP inspected. Uncovered front stoop allows bare lamp light to reach upstairs exterior frame without roof obstruction. Window glass is dark; ordinary adult/Zoe lineup and closed top-and-side shield with open lower face. Later pages must preserve this new house geometry.
visualReview.limits: Agent visual inspection, not classroom or physical-device evidence.
